headline: Highest risk is data leakage: cognee handles personal/finance data and can egress to allowlisted services, while ai-engineering-hub is an unverified MCP/RAG-oriented repo with no isolation details.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is an open-source repo tagged MCP/RAG/agents, so it plausibly emits or consumes instruction-like content. B stores session memory and supports multiple instances, which makes it plausible that A’s outputs could be ingested into B’s context. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF A is wired into B through a shared file, clipboard, or MCP bridge, prompt injection becomes actionable.
IF B treats imported text as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled content from A can steer behavior.
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all A outputs before B ingests them.
Disable automatic ingestion of A-generated text into B.
Require B to parse A outputs as data-only, not instructions.
Review any shared MCP or file bridge before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history, and it can call external APIs via LLM_API_KEY/COGNEE_SERVICE_URL. A has network_egress set to none, so it is less likely to exfiltrate directly, but the pair still creates a plausible leakage path if sensitive B data is fed into A or A’s outputs are forwarded onward.
conditions: IF B ingests personal or finance data and forwards it to external APIs, leakage occurs.
IF A is given sensitive B outputs through a shared workspace, those contents can be exposed in downstream processing.
mitigations: Do not route personal or finance data from B into A.
Restrict B API calls to redacted payloads.
Audit any shared workspace for sensitive files before use.
Turn off external connectors for test runs.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction and DLP at the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A shows no write or network capability beyond none egress, while B uses CLI with session memory and multiple instances. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write scope, so direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty is low because the profiles do not expose a common writable target.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or database, conflicts can emerge.
IF an orchestrator shares mutable state without locking, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same database or repo.
Use a lock file if a shared resource is unavoidable.
Run one agent at a time for mutation-heavy tasks.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s memory-oriented architecture can treat upstream text as durable context, and A is an agent/RAG-oriented repo that may generate structured outputs. If B consumes A’s output without verification, errors can cascade into decisions or workflows. No explicit verification barrier is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF B uses A output as input to decisions or workflows without validation, errors can propagate.
IF A emits hallucinated facts or malformed structure, B may persist them in session memory.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before B acts on A output.
Require schema validation on A outputs.
Limit A to draft-only mode.
Log and diff A outputs before ingestion.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or citation verification before downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles personal data and finance data, while A’s profile does not show residency or retention controls. Because the pair’s compliance posture is undocumented and B can call external APIs, a mismatch in retention or residency is plausible. I do not cite A-specific compliance fields because none are provided.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is routed through B’s external API calls, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF A is used to process data subject to residency or retention rules, the missing controls become relevant.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are confirmed.
Review retention settings on B.
Restrict external API use to non-sensitive data.
Document data flows for residency review.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for residency, retention, and deletion.
